[Weekly Album Discussion] Smash Mouth - Astro Lounge

Alright, I'm going to type this up as I'm listening to it so some of my ideas and opinions could radically change. Just hang on. Starts off interestingly, the the space-y thing at the start grabs my attention and then it kind of turns into a pretty middle of the road alt-rock tune. Pretty standard ABABCBB rock tune but it got my head bobbin a bit. Second tune, I like the distorted guitar that starts the track off but it kind of mellows out with the drum machine and what sounds like either a synth horn or synth guitar hit. Seems like a good "I'm playing video games" song that you leave on the background because the main melodies are fairly prominent and the lyrics aren't saying a whole lot. Now we slow waaay down to bring you this chilled out ballad. Kind of has a bit more punch at the chorus with their layered vocals but still kicks back to the verse with the laid back guitar strumming. Not gonna lie I could totally hear this song being played with a banjo and turned into a more bluegrass tune and it would probably sound like a good cover. I have a feeling this next track is going to get more intense. The slow guitar and distorted vocals makes me think there is going to be a drum fill soon. There we go. I was getting nervous there. Again it seems more like a background tune than a foreground tune. Either that or it could be the song to a sad moment from an early 2000's flick. Like in the rom-com when the girl loses interest in the guy and he rides the train back upstate. The phone ringing was kind of weird. Here's the song everyone knows. All Star baby. I think it's a good radio hit. Has easy to learn lyrics. Catchy beat. Easy to sing melody. Has the chorus that everyone can learn after the first listen so they can sing it the next time it comes around. The random aphorisms are an interesting touch. Kind of seems like it has a very deep meaning while not really delving too deep. It's like that uncle who always says things like "A bird in the hand is worth is worth two in the bush. A penny saved is a penny earned." You love him but you kind of know all he has to say. It's definitely got me nostalgic for my youth when I could just sit and watch Shrek instead of working 7-5. Satellite time. Has a sort of salsa feel to it with the shaker and now that echoey guitar. The lowered vocals kind of give the feel like some sultry spanish mistress singing to me. Not too bad. Again the music is more important than the lyrics and holy acoustic solo. Definitely reveals their spanish intent. Not saying that's a bad thing but it is definitely more obvious now. Here is a more punky start that kind of mellows out. I knew it wasn't going to be a true punk tune with it being 3 minutes. Kind of almost sounds like it could be a green day track. Like a dookie era green day song. Got a slow reggae/ska feel which is fitting for a song called Stoned. Feels like it might be a little inspired by Sublime maybe? I've never really listened to them before so I can't make a call. Then The Morning Comes has an americana feel to it. Like a sped up And Nothing Turned Itself Out track. Or a sped up track off of the latest Timber Timbre record. Gets a little surf rocky or beach boys-esque at the chorus. Has a very water park feel to me. There are just some songs sound like they could be played at a water park for me and pretty much anything from the early 2000's that have this kind of sound fall into that category. Here's another sort of reggae song. The vocals definitely add to the sound. Another sort of Americana feeling track. It's kind of a lazy track, I can hear what you are saying about the vibraphone on this track. It's definitely a different sound than we are used to but a lot of the other instruments are kind of par for the course. The distorted guitar, the synth, even the acoustic guitar at times is a bit typical for this genre. The last few tracks are kind of the same as before. No real new sounds that they try and explore. The last track is probably a good closer since it's very big and a good single. Though the tracks between that and Fallen horse kind of fall into a typical pattern.

I see the appeal that this can have to an extent. It's definitely falls into the trap of the singles out shining the other tracks. All star, Waste, and Can't Get Enough of You Baby are all very good and catchy songs. Just everything else seems to fall in the background or gets a little monotonous. The sounds aren't totally outlandish and they flirt with ideas for the intros of tracks but don't really follow through on them.

I love playing support. When I first started online gaming (WoW back in '07) I wanted to just do dmg so i did dps. then i went to tank and really fucking sucked, but throughout the years I got better. I started LoL back in 09 but could never do support. When FFXIV launched I started as BRD as I usually gravitated towards classes that had range. After completing the main story quest in game I decided to try WHM as I never really healed before, though I had back at the launch of Aion so I knew somewhat what to do. Now, to this day, I am all suport. I consider myself a rather good healer, also. I am doing both WHM and now AST (lvl 52) in it. I don't do WoW anymore as I gave it up. With HoTs out now (played since alpha) I really enjoy BW/LiLi/Malf. Long story short: I love support and it's not easy, play with a bad group and it's not a walk in the park.

I tend to play support a lot in MOBA and Team FPS games. I think a specific kind of person plays support. I don't have the instincts to play a more aggressive role in a MOBA: I don't know when to push, when to retreat, and when to poke. However, I find supporting someone else doing that role to be much more intuitive. Likewise, when I change it up and a friend who generally plays a more aggressive role plays support, they tend to approach it fundamentally differently with mixed success depending on the game.

As for FPS games, I am a much better FPS player than a MOBA player, but I still gravitate towards a support role a lot. In a shooter, it comes down more to understanding when/where to be and with what equipment rather than knowing which skill to use at which time. It is a much more similar skill-set to more aggressive roles due to less class diversity (with the exception of a few games).

Whit that in mind, I'm really interested in Blizzard's Overwatch because it looks like a FPS game that will be highly skill/character based like TF2. The first character I play will probably be a support class.

My Dota2 'pentagon' of skills is almost all balanced, except for support, which is definitely above average. I dont' know why I love playing support, i think it's because I have trust issues - I don't trust others to be able to ward, save, heal and buy the right items. Also, the feeling I get when I save people or help them get a kill is priceless. Obviously I get more abuse sometimes for feeding or not warding enough, but it's a small price to pay to win. Usually people are really appreciative too.
